artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p>3$ be a prime. Prove or disprove the following three congruences modulo $p^2$:

(1) $\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}\binom{4k}{2k+1}}{48^{k}}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{2}}.$

(2) If $p\equiv 1\pmod 3$ and $p=x^{2}+3y^{2}$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $x\equiv 1\pmod 3$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}\binom{4k}{2k}}{48^{k}}\equiv 2x-\frac{p}{2x}\pmod{p^{2}},$$
and moreover $x$ modulo $p^{2}$ is determined by
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k+1}{48^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}\binom{4k}{2k}\equiv x\pmod{p^{2}}.$$

(3) If $p\equiv 2\pmod 3$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}\binom{4k}{2k}}{48^{k}}\equiv 3p\binom{(p+1)/2}{(p+1)/6}\pmod{p^{2}}.$$

Here $\binom{n}{k}$ denotes the usual binomial coefficient, with the convention that $\binom{n}{k}=0$ if $k$ is not an integer in $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$, and the inverse $1/(2x)$ in (2) is taken modulo $p^{2}$.

While many related supercongruence conjectures of Z.-W. Sun have been proven by Guo, Mao and others, the present status of this particular conjecture could not be confirmed.
